title: GET /api/portfolio/risk — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #33 (api-portfolio-risk), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: docs/architecture/Backend.md's §2 module layout tree and §6 'Portfolio & Risk Engine' narrative don't mention the new app/portfolio/pricing.py module (EnrichedPosition/enrich_positions_with_price/positions_value) added by this PR and now shared by both GET /api/portfolio and GET /api/portfolio/risk. Not a violation of any documented layering principle (it fits the existing portfolio/ package correctly, imports only from data/db/portfolio.models, and is imported only by the api/ layer), but the diagram and narrative should be updated for accuracy -- same category of gap as the api-portfolio-get-followups task's analogous finding about app/api/dependencies.py missing from the same diagram.

In get_risk()'s first pass loop (app/api/routers/portfolio.py), provider.get_weekly_ohlcv(ticker) is fetched before protective_stop() is attempted. A position whose daily frame fails protective_stop's validation (missing column, too short) still pays for a weekly fetch (a network/cache round trip) that gets thrown away once the daily side excludes it. Swap the order -- attempt protective_stop() first, only fetch weekly on success -- to avoid the wasted I/O for positions that are ultimately excluded on the daily side.

comments.summary: docs/architecture/Backend.md's new portfolio/pricing.py paragraph says it depends only on data/base.py's DataProvider protocol and db/models.py/portfolio/models.py, but pricing.py also imports DataProviderError from app.data.exceptions (used in _latest_close's except clause). Minor inaccuracy, non-blocking. Tracked as a checklist item on docs/tasks/api-portfolio-risk-followups-followups.json.

The get_risk() reorder (protective_stop() before provider.get_weekly_ohlcv()) is behavior-preserving and verified correct by inspection and by the full test suite, but no test pins down the intended effect itself -- that the weekly fetch is now skipped for a position excluded on the daily side. Existing integration tests all supply valid weekly data even for daily-excluded positions, so they'd pass identically with or without the reorder. Non-blocking; tracked as a checklist item on docs/tasks/api-portfolio-risk-followups-followups.json.

review.notes: Verified: checked out PR #34 (task/api-portfolio-risk-followups). Full backend suite: 397 passed, coverage 99.64% (gate 90%), app/api/routers/portfolio.py and app/portfolio/pricing.py both at 100%. No ruff/mypy configured in backend/pyproject.toml so none run (matches project config). No route/schema signature change so no openapi.json regen required. No frontend/UI surface touched by this PR (docs + internal loop-ordering only) -- browser walkthrough explicitly skipped as inapplicable. code-review skill (medium effort) found no correctness bugs or reuse/simplification/efficiency issues. Manually traced the get_risk() reorder: protective_stop() has no side effects and both try/except blocks independently gate inclusion in `stops`/`weekly_by_id`, so swapping their order changes only which I/O is skipped when the daily side excludes a position, not the final set of included positions -- confirmed behavior-preserving. Confirmed the Backend.md addition is accurate: pricing.py is imported only from app/api/routers/portfolio.py (plus its own unit test), matching the 'imported only from the api/ layer' claim; flagged one minor omission (data/exceptions.py) in the dependency list, non-blocking. Two non-blocking findings recorded above and filed as checklist items on docs/tasks/api-portfolio-risk-followups-followups.json (new follow-up task, since none existed yet for this task id).
